newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Yeltsin agree to meet in March.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin agree to meet in March.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin agreed on Thursday to meet in March but did not set a date or venue, the White House said.

The two men spoke by telephone for about 20 minutes on Thursday morning, with Clinton expressing his pleasure at Yeltsin's recovery from heart bypass surgery and the Russian president congratulating Clinton on his re-election.
White House officials said it was the U.S. turn to host the summit because Clinton and Yeltsin last met, in April, in Moscow.
But they said because of Yeltsin's health, it was possible they might meet in a third country closer to Russia or even in Moscow.
Thursday's telephone conversation was the first between the two since Yeltsin's quintuple heart bypass surgery and Clinton's re-election, both on Nov. 5.

"The two leaders agreed on the importance of their joint leadership in further strengthening the U.S.-Russian relationship and in dealing with a wide range of issues on the bilateral agenda," the White House said in a brief statement.
In Moscow, a Russian presidential spokesman confirmed a report by Russia's Interfax news agency that the two men would meet in March, but gave no further details.

The White House did not immediately say what topics would be on the agenda, but they are likely to include expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) and a variety of bilateral subjects.
The statement said a meeting between U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomydrin in February would lay the groundwork for the summit.

At their April meeting in Moscow, Clinton and Yeltsin spoke for five hours on a series of security issues, among them arms control, nuclear proliferation and NATO expansion, which Russia has historically opposed.
In October, Clinton said he wanted new members to join the western security alliance by 1999, the 50th anniversary of its founding.
Although he did not specify which countries might be invited to join first, they are expected to be the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.
